newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Japan talent firm aims to boost profile.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Japan talent firm aims to boost profile.

text.p: Japanese talent agency Horipro Inc hopes to boost its profile by listing on the main section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in about five years' time.
"I think it's going to be about five years from now," chairman Takeo Hori said, when asked in an interview with Reuters about the company's target for listing on the first section.
The 38-year-old talent agency, famous in Japan for its star-studded clientele, has attracted attention recently by branching into cyberspace to create "virtual" pop sensation Kyoko Date.

"I've always dreamed of a talent who doesn't age, fall sick or create a scandal. Walt Disney's characters are like that. The recent advancements in computer technology have led us to conceive this 'virtual idol', who is very close to the ideal," Hori said.
Hori said a first-section listing would boost the company's profile and show that the company is on an expansion path.
Horipro's shares are already listed on the second section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

Hori said that he wants to foster a corporate culture that encourages staff to tackle new projects such as the recent one that enabled the company to use the latest computer graphics technology to create the virtual teen idol.
Since making her debut in November, Date, whose voice is dubbed by an actress, has won fans with an one-hour radio show aired weekly on a Tokyo FM station.
Hori said Date had attracted the interest of entertainment industries abroad and has received invitations from foreign companies for her to perform.
Date receives tons of letters from fans, who can also opt to buy CD-ROMs showcasing the virtual idol's singing and dancing, a Horipro spokesman said.

Although its virtual idol project has not brought profits to the company yet, Hori remains optimistic, as the launch of multi-channel digital satellite broadcasting, which is just starting to catch on in Japan, will increase demand for more programmes and stars.
Hori said that a "virtual drama" featuring Date and her family members could be aired through one of the satellite channels in the future.
Horipro currently manages 115 stars in Japan. The only other talent agency listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange is Osaka-based Yoshimoto Kogyo Co Ltd.
